review_candidates.title: District Coordinator
review_candidates.description: Company Description FOUNDATION TO EDUCATE GIRLS GLOBALLY is a hospital and health care organization headquartered in New Delhi, India, with operations that support community-focused health and education initiatives. The organization works to improve health outcomes by strengthening access to services and promoting awareness, particularly among underserved populations. Team members collaborate closely with local stakeholders, government bodies, and partners to implement programs that create sustainable impact. The foundation values integrity, inclusivity, and a mission-driven approach in all aspects of its work, offering professionals the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to community development. Role Description The District Coordinator is a full-time, on-site role based in Lucknow, responsible for overseeing the implementation of health and education initiatives at the district level. This role involves coordinating with local authorities, schools, health facilities, and community organizations to ensure effective program delivery and alignment with organizational goals. The District Coordinator will plan and monitor district-level activities, manage data collection and reporting, and support training and capacity-building efforts for field teams and partners. The position requires regular field visits, stakeholder meetings, and problem-solving to address on-ground challenges, as well as preparing periodic progress reports and recommendations for program improvement. The role also includes supporting budgeting and resource allocation within the district, and ensuring compliance with organizational policies and local regulations. Qualifications Demonstrated experience in program coordination or project management within the health, education, or social development sectors. Strong skills in stakeholder engagement, including working with government agencies, community leaders, and partner organizations. Ability to collect, analyze, and interpret program data, and prepare clear reports and presentations for internal and external audiences. Proficiency in planning, organizing, and monitoring multiple activities, with attention to timelines, quality standards, and outcomes. Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; fluency in Hindi or local languages is highly beneficial. Comfort with on-site field work, including regular travel within the district and direct engagement with communities. Bachelor’s degree in public health, social work, education, management, or a related field; a master’s degree is an advantage. Ability to work independently and as part of a team, with a strong commitment to equity, inclusion, and community impact. Basic to intermediate proficiency with office productivity tools (e.g., word processing, spreadsheets, presentations) for documentation and reporting.

review_candidates.title: Director, HR Technology & Data
review_candidates.description: Who We Are International Justice Mission (IJM) is the global leader in protecting vulnerable people from violence around the world. Our team of over 1,200 professionals are at work worldwide in over 30 offices. Together we are on a mission to rescue millions, protect half a billion, and make justice unstoppable. We are a global community that cares for one another. We believe that the way we work is as important as the results we achieve. We provide professional excellence with joy and celebration to all those we serve. The Need For over 25 years, IJM has pioneered the work to protect vulnerable people from violence. 9 out of 9 times in the last decade, IJM’s Justice System Strengthening Projects have reduced slavery and violence between 50 and 85% for very large populations of people in poverty. As we grow to expand our impact to protect 500 million people from violence, we are seeking a Director, HR Technology & Data to work closely with the VP, HR Operations to provide strategic leadership and governance for IJM’s global HR technology ecosystem, people data strategy, and workforce analytics. They will serve as the key advisor to HR and business leadership on workforce insights, HR systems, data governance, compliance, and technology innovation. This role partners closely with leaders across Global People Support (GPS), Global Finance, Global Technology Solutions (GTS), Global Risk & Legal (GRL), and regional leadership teams to enhance organizational effectiveness through data-driven decision-making and scalable technology solutions. Manages a global team of analysts and specialists to ensure effectiveness of systems and processes to deliver operational excellence. This position is hybrid (onsite Tuesdays & Thursdays) if located in the Washington, DC area or remote for non-local candidates. It reports to the Vice President, HR Operations and requires current authorization to work in the United States. Visa sponsorship is not available for this position, now or in the future. Responsibilities: HR Technology Strategy & Governance: Develops and executes a comprehensive global HR technology strategy that is aligned with organizational priorities and owns the long-term roadmap for Workday and related HR systems and tools; Establishes governance frameworks for and manages system configurations, security, integrations, release cycles, and all facets of change management including but not limited to testing and user acceptance testing and training; Leads and collaborates on enterprise-wide HR technology transformation and projects, driving implementation, adoption, and ensuring alignment with the broader enterprise technology strategy; and Evaluates emerging technologies (i.e. AI-enabled HR solutions and automation) to improve employee and manager experience, ensuring all platforms support compliance, security, and operational excellence. People Analytics & Workforce Intelligence: Establishes a global people analytics strategy that supports workforce planning and decision-making, inclusive of predictive and descriptive analytics to monitor, identify, and assess workforce trends, risks, and opportunities; Leads the development of informative dashboards that translate workforce data into meaningful insights that drive recommendations to/for leadership (i.e. attrition, engagement, rewards, etc.); and Supports the building of a data-driven, evidence-based culture of decision making across GPS and IJM leadership as well as data literacy among HRPBs and managers. Leadership: Leads a global team responsible for HR Systems, reporting, analytics and data governance, providing strategic direction, coaching, and professional development to team members; Creates a high-performance culture focused on innovation, customer service, and continuous improvement; and Leads the development of global standards of data protection (inclusive of security and access), policies, definitions, and processes ensuring compliance with all laws and regulations governing cross-border data sharing. Collaboration and Teamwork: Serves as a trusted advisor to leadership on workforce metrics, and HR technology investments and trends; Leads and/or participate on cross-functional teams to lend subject matter expertise for the accomplishment of goals; Collaborate with GTS and GPS leadership to identify and address system needs and enhancements; Collaborate with Global Finance on the delivery of interdependent processes and projects; Partners with GRL on HR Data Protection Policy and Processes; and Educates and trains system users on the effective use of self-service options and escalation protocols. General Tasks: Participate in IJM’s community of spiritual formation. Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree or certification in Information Technology, Information Systems, or equivalent combination of education and experience; Ten years of progressive experience in HR Technology, HR Operations, HRIS, People Analytics, or similar; Substantive experience supporting a multi-country workforce and the associated data protection laws; Minimum five years people leadership experience; Demonstrated success leading enterprise Workday implementations, deployments, and optimization programs; Experience developing workforce analytics strategies and reporting frameworks; Workday HCM certifications; Workday systems configuration, advanced reporting, and integration tools; Experience with data visualization tools (i.e. Power BI, Tableu, etc.); Experience leading technical projects; Experience writing UAT criteria or scripts for technical system requirements; High proficiency in report writing and data/statistical analysis; and Advanced proficiency with data protection methods and laws. Critical Qualities: Eager commitment to IJM’s Core Values: Christian, Professional and Bridge-Building; Strong customer service orientation and practical problem-solving behaviors are required; Demonstrated ability to conceptualize, analyze, and explain complex and abstract problems in lay terms; Demonstrated ability to manage multiple or competing priorities and work in a fast-paced environment; Demonstrated ability to manage cross-cultural relationships; and Demonstrated ability to influence without formal authority. Application Process: Upload Resume, Cover Letter & Statement of Faith* in one PDF document. What is a statement of faith? A statement of faith should describe your Christian faith and how you see it as relevant to your involvement with IJM. The statement can either be incorporated into the cover letter or submitted as a separate document and should include, at a minimum, a description of your spiritual disciplines (prayer, study, etc.) and your current fellowship or place of worship. What does IJM have to offer? Comprehensive Medical/Dental/Vision benefits Monthly commuter and parking benefits in the DC metro area Retirement benefit options Paid leave starting at 23 days 12 holidays (plus early release the day prior) Daily, quarterly, and annual community spiritual formation Robust staff care resources IJM holds strict safeguarding principles and a zero tolerance to violations of the Safeguarding Policy, Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment Policy, and Code of Ethics. Candidate selection is based on technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring criteria subject to assessing the candidate’s value congruence and thorough background, police clearance, and reference check processes. At IJM, we’re committed to building a diverse workforce through fair and equitable employment practices. IJM encourages people of any race, color, age, sex, marital status or political ideology to apply for employment. While we welcome everyone into this work, we truly believe that the work we are doing is God’s work, not our own, and practice spiritual disciplines together daily. That’s why we legally require under SEC. 2000e-1 [Section702] of Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 that all employees practice a mature orthodox Christian faith, as defined by the Apostles’ Creed. IJM requires a background check, police clearance and thorough review of references with an employment offer and/or employment contract.

review_candidates.title: Director, Communications at Women's Equality Center
review_candidates.description: At Women's Equality Center (WEC), we work behind the scenes supporting the people and organizations fighting for reproductive freedom on the ground—offering critical communications and campaign strategy support right where it's most urgently needed. About The Organization WEC is a political strategy organization that uses communications as a key tool to advance reproductive health, rights, and justice across Latin America and the Caribbean. Operating across 9 countries—Mexico, Brazil, Colombia, Honduras, the Dominican Republic, Argentina, Chile, El Salvador, and Uruguay—we build bridges between LATAM and the U.S. through grants, integrated policy and communications campaigns, and rapid-response operations. Rather than focusing on our own branding, we let our local partners lead as the experts on the ground while we work alongside them to build adaptable, big-picture messaging frameworks around emerging political opportunities. Guided by a deeply collaborative, ego-free, and agile approach, we bring together diverse perspectives to drive pragmatic policy wins and strengthen the broader movement for reproductive freedom. As an organization, WEC prioritizes a collaborative environment, allowing for flexibility in the structure among teams and roles. We aim to keep boundaries between roles flexible to ensure that we're bringing the full range of expertise, experience, and perspective of every team member to the strategies we're developing and work we're doing. Everyone does a little bit of everything here - no job is too small. We've worked very hard to establish an organizational culture based on collaboration, candor, transparency, mutual respect, and trust. We take these values very seriously and expect that of any new member of our team. For more information, please visit our website. About The Role What You'll Do The Director, Communications will serve as one of two directors leading WEC's communications and media operations across the Latin America and Caribbean region. Working in close collaboration with the Executive Team which includes the Executive Director, Chief Program Officer, and Chief Advocacy Officer and WEC's Communications, Policy, and Programs teams, the incoming Director will support WEC's on-the-ground partners as a critical strategic adviser. In today's rapidly evolving media landscape—where traditional press has shifted and digital influencers and algorithmic challenges require bold, defensive, and creative thinking—you will design and execute multi-channel communications strategies, campaigns, and tactics. By capitalizing on emerging political opportunities, you will work to shift narratives, influence public perspectives, and ultimately drive pragmatic, positive policy changes in reproductive and abortion access across the region. This is an ideal opportunity for a bilingual, 360-degree communications strategist with a strong policy lens who values creative risk-taking and quick thinking, thrives in ambiguity, and is committed to supporting organizations on the front lines of reproductive freedom. Key Responsibilities Communications Strategy and Partnership Collaboration Support WEC's Executive Team, peer Director, and Policy Leads in refining WEC's communications strategy framework into one that leverages opportunities and mitigates for risks in a fast-changing political landscape while allowing us to set proactive and future thinking communications strategies Design and execute compelling, locally relevant communications strategies (in English and Spanish), working closely with in-country partners and WEC's political and digital leads to amplify the impact of our campaigns Identify areas in which WEC's collaboration with partners on policy and strategic communications campaigns could catalyze significant progress, or serve critical defensive roles Coordinate and support potential lobbying initiatives executed through our 501(c)(4) arm, GISWF/WECAF, ensuring strategic alignment across policy and partner advocacy efforts Monitor broader developments across the Latin America and Caribbean region for opportunities, challenges, and threats with regard to reproductive rights, health, and justice Provide robust analyses of the media, political, public opinion, landscapes in target regions, countries, and localities Set detailed proposals for tactics, timelines, and budgets, and report out progress of work to relevant and key stakeholders, including the ED, Advisory Committee, and funders Team Leadership Model WEC's values and serves as a culture carrier fostering an inclusive and collaborative environment for all who work in, with, and alongside WEC Participate in driving broader organizational strategy and direction acting as a thought leader and leveraging your communications expertise to assist in formulating future initiatives and approaches Serve as an organizational ambassador ensuring positive, effective, and collaborative working relationships across in-country organizations and teams Support the hiring, management, and development of in-house staff and external consultants with a focus on ensuring each person is well-positioned to achieve their goals Ensure the effective deployment of capital, people, and resources across communications projects Who You'll Work With You will report to a member of the Executive Team which includes the Executive Director, Chief Program Officer, and Chief Advocacy Officer You will frequently collaborate with the peer Director of Communications You will partner closely with other members of the communications team including Directors, Managers, Associate Directors, and Coordinators You will supervise project teams and in-country colleagues across specific communications work Required Skills And Experience A Note to Potential Candidates Studies have shown that women, trans, non-binary folks, and BIPOC are less likely to apply for jobs unless they believe they meet every single one of the qualifications as described in a job description. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive organization, and we are most interested in finding the best candidate for the job. That candidate may be one who comes from a background less traditional to our field of work, and that's okay. We would strongly encourage you to apply, even if you don't believe you meet every one of the qualifications described. Please note that part of the selection process will be conducted in Spanish. Please Apply If You Are Proactive and entrepreneurial, someone who brings passion and drive, and is not afraid to take risks A multi-tasker and proactive prioritizer, someone who is energized by working on many things at once, yet able to sort through the important from the unimportant Humble but with a strong sense of self and the ability to hold others accountable to achieve goals Additional Qualifications Include Professional fluency in Spanish and English; ability to communicate with depth and nuance in writing and conversation in both languages (required) 10+ years of strategic communications experience ideally in the development, management, and execution of communications strategies for advancing progressive policy. This can include: Supporting litigation, community organizing, and other defensive actions, and/or influencing public opinion and catalyzing action on issues of reproductive health/rights/justice or social justice more generally at a social sector organization or agency Prior work on Capitol Hill or a U.S.-based political campaign Ability to work with a multi-cultural, multi-lingual, and deeply collaborative workforce, and a sensitivity and appreciation of cultural differences An understanding of Latin America and the Caribbean, including insight into the politics, public opinion landscape, and coalition dynamics of key countries with regard to issues of reproductive and social justice is highly preferred but not required Prior international experience strongly preferred (ideally across Latin America and the Caribbean) Excellent verbal and written skills with a track record of delivering strong written materials and presentations, including press releases, memos, op eds, social media content, crisis communication, proposals, and strategic plans Can work successfully and collaborative with a variety of internal and external stakeholders and contributes their expertise to broader organizational planning and vision scoping Ideally brings experience with coalition and partnership building Has managed small teams and has overseen consultant engagements ensuring strong project outcomes Efficiency and comfort with technology, including Slack, Google Suite, CRMs; responsiveness via email and WhatsApp, and willingness to participate in weekly group calls or as needed The above job description is not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties and skills required for the position. The incoming Director may be required to perform duties outside of their normal responsibilities from time to time, as needed. Additional Details Employment Status Full-time (40 hours), Exempt. Flexible Work Environment Women's Equality Center is a flexible/remote working environment, with team members working across the United States and Latin America. However, this is a U.S.-based position and U.S. work authorization is required. Visa sponsorship is not available. Compensation The salary range for this position is $150,000 to $161,534. Where someone lands within this range will be dependent on years of experience and alignment to the necessary skills required for the role. Please note that WEC utilizes a points-based offer system to determine specific compensation. This philosophy was created to ensure equity in staff compensation and to eliminate bias. WEC will make their best offer upfront and as such will not negotiate on salary. Travel The Director will be expected to travel (including internationally), up to 50% of the time, some of which may occur over weekends or holidays. Global Impact Ventures Careers Women's Equality Center is a project of Global Impact Ventures (c3), a nonprofit that works with nonprofit, public, and private sector clients. and Global Impact Social Welfare Fund, a 501(c)(4) that supports philanthropic fund processing and distribution for education and advocacy addressing public policy issues. At Global Impact, we passionately celebrate our culture, values, and community. We are committed to cultivating and nurturing a workplace for all. Global Impact encourages ALL interested candidates to apply for this position.
